1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Technique for an adaptive exam. Look-alike pairs. Numbers and facts to memorize. Five questions to ask in every scenario. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All domains: adaptive exam technique, numbers to memorize, look-alike terms and decision rules. Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Technique for an adaptive exam
1.text: Technique for an adaptive exam. Format. one hundred to one hundred twenty-five items in two hours, no item review; answer each item as it comes. Difficulty. Items aim at a fifty percent chance of a right answer, so expect them to feel hard. Pretest items. twenty-five items do not count and look the same: treat every item seriously. Time. About one minute per item; do not stall; never leave a blank. Length. A longer exam is not a bad sign. Method. Last line first, find the domain, eliminate two answers, pick the best one. Exam tip: Two answers are usually wrong at once. Then ask "which is preventive, within policy, least privilege, and the first step?".

1.title: Look-alike pairs
1.text: Look-alike pairs. Due care and due diligence. Act and maintain and investigate first. Policy, standard, procedure, guideline. What and why, which, how, optional advice. R T O and R P O. Time to be back and data you can lose. B C P and D R P. Keep the business running and restore I T. Vulnerability scan and penetration test. Find weaknesses and exploit them. Phishing, spear phishing, whaling. Many, one person, an executive. Rogue A P and evil twin. Unauthorized device and fake copy of a real network. Stateless and stateful firewall. Each packet alone and remembers connections.

1.title: Look-alike pairs, continued
1.text: Look-alike pairs. I D S and I P S. Alert and block. D A C, M A C, R back, A B A C. Owner, labels, roles, attributes. Po L P and So D. How much access and who completes a task. Symmetric, asymmetric, hash. One key, key pair, no key. Masking and sanitization. Hide part of a value and remove data from media. K P I and K R I. Performance and early warning. True positive, false positive, false negative. Real alert, harmless alert, missed attack. Inherent and residual risk. Before controls and after controls.

1.title: Numbers and facts to memorize
1.text: Numbers and facts to memorize. Exam. one hundred to one hundred twenty-five items, two hours, seven hundred of one thousand, twenty-five unscored, at least seventy-five scored. Domain weights. twenty-four, seventeen point three, twenty, twenty-one point three, seventeen point three percent. Risk formulas. S L E equals A V times E F; A L E equals S L E times A R O. Risk treatments. Avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept. I R phases. Prepare, detect and analyze, contain, eradicate, recover, learn. Ports. S S H twenty-two, Telnet twenty-three, D N S fifty-three, H T T P eighty, H T T P S four forty-three, R D P thirty-three eighty-nine.

1.title: Numbers and facts to memorize, continued
1.text: Numbers and facts to memorize. O S I. seven layers; router three, switch two, port four. I P. I P version four thirty-two bits, I P version six one hundred twenty-eight bits. Cloud. five characteristics, I A A S, pass, sass, customer always owns data and access. Code of Ethics. four canons in order: society first. Exam tip: Review the lists you can rattle off: C I A, A A A, I R phases, life cycle steps, cloud characteristics, canons.

1.title: Five questions to ask in every scenario
1.text: Five questions to ask in every scenario. Which goal is at stake? (confidentiality, integrity, availability). Finds the control family. Which domain is it? Finds the right vocabulary. What is the first step? Many answers are too late. Is it least privilege and policy-based? The safe default. Is it preventive and simple? Prefer prevent over fix. Exam tip: If you do not know, eliminate the extreme answers (do nothing, ignore policy, the most drastic fix) and choose the measured, policy-based answer.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A candidate reaches item one hundred and the exam continues. What does this mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The system needs more items to be confident. After the minimum length the exam continues until the system is ninety-five percent confident or a limit is reached; a longer exam is not a sign of failure.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which two terms describe how much data can be lost and how long recovery may take? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: R P O for data loss and R T O for recovery time. The recovery point objective is acceptable data loss and the recovery time objective is the time to restore.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A user needs temporary access to a system to fix an issue. What principle guides the grant? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Least privilege, with only needed access. Grant only the needed access for the needed time.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which control type is a security awareness training program? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Administrative, because it is a people and policy control. Training is an administrative control.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company stores its web shop in a public cloud virtual machine. Who patches the guest operating system? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The customer. In I A A S the customer manages and patches the operating system.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An analyst finds that an incident is spreading between servers. What is the best next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Contain it by isolating the affected servers. Containment limits the spread before eradication and recovery.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the passing grade? Answer: seven hundred out of one thousand. Question two. Which domain is the largest? Answer: Security Principles, twenty-four percent. Question three. What are the C I A goals? Answer: Confidentiality, integrity, availability.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the identity life cycle stages? Answer: Roles definition, provision, review, deprovision. Question five. What does zero trust say? Answer: Never trust, always verify. Question six. Who decides data classification? Answer: The data owner.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Method: last line, domain, eliminate, preventive and policy-based answer. Adaptive: one hundred to one hundred twenty-five items, no review, twenty-five unscored, longer is not worse. Look-alikes: due care versus diligence, R T O versus R P O, scan versus pen test, I D S versus I P S. Defaults: least privilege, first step, contain before eradicate, customer owns data. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
